chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to 900 seconds, but the old behavior—stated in the knob’s own doc as “0 sweeps on every brief, as before”—was to run `dispose_finished` on every `brief`. On an upgraded repo with finished leftover worktrees and no `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last`, `ddflow brief` will now skip the sweep for up to 15 minutes instead of sweeping immediately. This violates [r-everything-configurable], which requires a new knob to default to the old behavior; the default should be 0 (with cadence opt-in).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:sweep_interval_s

chunk_findings.detail: `prefetch_on_base` runs `git rev-list --no-walk <chunk> ^<base> --` and treats every printed object id as “base lacks this commit.” But `--no-walk` deliberately does not traverse ancestors of a negative revision: if `<A>` is an ancestor of `<base>`, `git rev-list --no-walk <A> ^<base>` still prints `<A>`. So a worktree whose HEAD is `<A>`, already reachable from the base, leads `prefetch_on_base(["<A>"], "<base>")` to cache `_on_base[(<A>, <base>)]` as `False`, and a later `on_base("<A>", "<base>")` returns `False` when the true answer is `True` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <A> <base>` exits 0). The code comment’s claim that this prints “exactly the listed commits the base lacks” is false, and the wrong reachability answer can drive an incorrect finished/sweep classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py: RepoFacts.prefetch_on_base

chunk_findings.detail: With the new default `lease.scan_view_trees_max = 16` and the stated 126 stale leases in the falsifier, `_measure` will measure 16 worktrees. For each measured tree it calls `W.tree_work(wt, base, ahead=False)` for dirty files and then `facts.ahead(wt, base)` for the ahead count. Those are two git subprocesses per measured tree, so just these calls produce 32 subprocesses before the initial `RepoFacts` queries. That makes the change's own falsifier "more than 30 git subprocesses for status with 126 stale leases" true, not false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_measure

chunk_findings.detail: The note records `new = "16"`. The pre-change `_measure` this diff replaces had no cap: status/brief measured every stale worktree. A repository with 17 stale worktrees therefore changes from measuring all 17 to measuring 16 and marking the 17th as NOT MEASURED. That is not the old behaviour, contradicting the change's CONFORMANCE claim that "a new knob defaults to the old behaviour"; it is a semantic behaviour change for existing users, not merely additive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:new

chunk_findings.detail: The submitted CONFORMANCE clause states “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour”, but neither new knob in this part does: `worktree.sweep_interval_s` defaults to `900`, while the old behavior was a sweep on every `brief` (only `0` restores that behavior), and `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` defaults to `0`, while the old status/brief behavior was to weigh all such items (only a value above 0 restores that path). A repository upgraded with no config changes therefore gets the new behavior immediately: finished worktrees are not swept for up to 15 minutes, and status/brief no longer do the old full scan. This contradicts the stated [r-upgrade-safe] default-compatibility criterion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:6 and ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test hard-codes the default read-only view cap as 16: `assert sum(1 for r in capped if r.salvageable is None) == 20 - 16`. Since `view=True` is the read-only path used by `RP.status`, a default `status` on the stated 126-stale-lease scenario will measure only 16 leases and leave 110 as “NOT MEASURED”. That conflicts with the CONFORMANCE requirement that the new `lease.scan_view_trees_max` knob defaults to the old behaviour; old `status` measured every expired lease, so the default must be uncapped. Either conforming code fails this assertion, or the shipped default violates the requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py::test_recover_still_measures_every_tree

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `LC.brief` twice without setting `worktree.sweep_interval_s`, then asserts only one `sweep_finished` call. chunk_findings.detail: `_sweep_stamp(repo)` is now called before `CL.sweep_finished`. Before this change `CL.sweep_finished` ran first, so a stamp-write failure only caused a later retry; now a transient or permission problem with the stamp file can silently disable the sweep for the current and future due checks.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob still defaults to `new = "900"`, while the old behaviour was a sweep on every brief (`0`). chunk_findings.detail: The note now says "Default-behaviour change" in `why`, but all three modified upgrade notes still set `impact = "additive"`. A default-behaviour change for existing repos is not additive: an upgraded repo with 17 stale worktrees sees the 17th reported NOT MEASURED under the new default with no config change. Upgrade tooling that uses `impact` to classify breaking changes will not flag this note, which contradicts r-docs-with-change. chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `LC.brief` twice without setting `worktree.sweep_interval_s`, then asserts exactly one `sweep_finished` call. chunk_findings.detail: `branch_tip_aheads` interpolates `base` directly into a `git for-each-ref` format atom with `f"--format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:{base})"`. Git branch/ref names may legally contain a closing parenthesis, e.g. `release/1.0)`. A status scan over 126 stale leases whose worktrees point at 31 or more distinct branch tips then spawns more than 30 git subprocesses, contradicting this change’s FALSIFIER and the module docstring’s “one for-each-ref per command”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:_tip_aheads

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #6 still holds. `new = "16"` plus `impact = "additive"` does not preserve the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe]: before this change `status`/`brief` measured every stale worktree, while `_measure` now stops after the budget (`lease.scan_view_trees_max`) is exhausted and marks the rest `salvageable = None` / NOT MEASURED. A repo with 17 stale clean worktrees and no config change will no longer have the 17th tree measured on upgrade, so the upgrade note misclassifies this as additive. The triage probe (`test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes`) does not answer this: it passes by exercising the 16-tree cap and counting subprocesses, not by verifying that a 17th stale clean worktree is still measured.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to `900`, but the old `brief` swept finished worktrees on every invocation. The change’s own CONFORMANCE text requires “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour” [r-upgrade-safe], and this note says the old per-call sweep is restored only by setting `0`; `impact = "additive"` therefore misclassifies a user-visible behavior change. Concrete failure: on an existing project upgraded with no config change, run `brief`, finish a worktree, then run `brief` again within 900 seconds; the second run skips the sweep the prior code would have performed. The triage probe `test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes` counts subprocess spawns and does not exercise the sweep cadence, so it does not answer this.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` knob defaults to `0`, which disables the previous status/brief full verdict scan. This violates the CONFORMANCE requirement that a new knob default to the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe]; the note’s own `why` says status and brief “no longer weigh the full completion” and “set above 0 to restore it”, so it is a behavior change, not `impact = "additive"`. Concrete failure: on an existing project with a merged-but-unfinished lease, run `status` after upgrading with no config change; it no longer weighs completion for any item, whereas the pre-change `status` did. chunk_findings.detail: The test’s own docstring says an unknown commit is “could not tell”, not “not an ancestor”, yet it asserts `f.on_base("0" * 40, "main") is False`. In this tri-state API `False` is the off-base value; the correct unknown result must be `None` (the module docstring says unknown is never a guess). This test therefore codifies the bug from previous finding 2 and would fail once `on_base` returns `None` for exit 128. The author’s probe passes only because the production code returns the `False` this test demands, not because the contract is met.

chunk_findings.detail: These tests assert that two immediate `LC.brief` runs on an unconfigured repo invoke `sweep_finished` only once (`len(calls) == 1`). The change’s CONFORMANCE clause requires “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour”, and the previous `brief` swept finished worktrees on every call, so the default must be `0`. The author’s triage for previous finding 9 only runs the status subprocess-count probe, which does not exercise this default; the upgrade-safety violation remains and these tests lock it in.

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` on line 127 and returns `False` on line 128 when true. However, line 128 returns `False` which exits the function immediately, so the subsequent cache assignment `self._on_base[key] = r.ok` on line 131 is correctly skipped for non-zero/non-one codes, but the return statement on line 128 returns `False`, which means "is an ancestor" returns `False` (meaning "not on base") when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails with 128 (unknown commit). A caller querying `on_base` for a non-existent or unknown commit receives `False` instead of an indication of failure or unavailability, causing the system to treat an unknown commit as definitively not an ancestor.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to 900 seconds, but the old behavior—stated in the knob’s own doc as “0 sweeps on every brief, as before”—was to run `dispose_finished` on every `brief`. On an upgraded repo with finished leftover worktrees and no `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last`, `ddflow brief` will now skip the sweep for up to 15 minutes instead of sweeping immediately. This violates [r-everything-configurable], which requires a new knob to default to the old behavior; the default should be 0 (with cadence opt-in).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:sweep_interval_s

chunk_findings.detail: `prefetch_on_base` runs `git rev-list --no-walk <chunk> ^<base> --` and treats every printed object id as “base lacks this commit.” But `--no-walk` deliberately does not traverse ancestors of a negative revision: if `<A>` is an ancestor of `<base>`, `git rev-list --no-walk <A> ^<base>` still prints `<A>`. So a worktree whose HEAD is `<A>`, already reachable from the base, leads `prefetch_on_base(["<A>"], "<base>")` to cache `_on_base[(<A>, <base>)]` as `False`, and a later `on_base("<A>", "<base>")` returns `False` when the true answer is `True` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <A> <base>` exits 0). The code comment’s claim that this prints “exactly the listed commits the base lacks” is false, and the wrong reachability answer can drive an incorrect finished/sweep classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py: RepoFacts.prefetch_on_base

chunk_findings.detail: With the new default `lease.scan_view_trees_max = 16` and the stated 126 stale leases in the falsifier, `_measure` will measure 16 worktrees. For each measured tree it calls `W.tree_work(wt, base, ahead=False)` for dirty files and then `facts.ahead(wt, base)` for the ahead count. Those are two git subprocesses per measured tree, so just these calls produce 32 subprocesses before the initial `RepoFacts` queries. That makes the change's own falsifier "more than 30 git subprocesses for status with 126 stale leases" true, not false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_measure

chunk_findings.detail: The note records `new = "16"`. The pre-change `_measure` this diff replaces had no cap: status/brief measured every stale worktree. A repository with 17 stale worktrees therefore changes from measuring all 17 to measuring 16 and marking the 17th as NOT MEASURED. That is not the old behaviour, contradicting the change's CONFORMANCE claim that "a new knob defaults to the old behaviour"; it is a semantic behaviour change for existing users, not merely additive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:new

chunk_findings.detail: The submitted CONFORMANCE clause states “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour”, but neither new knob in this part does: `worktree.sweep_interval_s` defaults to `900`, while the old behavior was a sweep on every `brief` (only `0` restores that behavior), and `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` defaults to `0`, while the old status/brief behavior was to weigh all such items (only a value above 0 restores that path). A repository upgraded with no config changes therefore gets the new behavior immediately: finished worktrees are not swept for up to 15 minutes, and status/brief no longer do the old full scan. This contradicts the stated [r-upgrade-safe] default-compatibility criterion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:6 and ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test hard-codes the default read-only view cap as 16: `assert sum(1 for r in capped if r.salvageable is None) == 20 - 16`. Since `view=True` is the read-only path used by `RP.status`, a default `status` on the stated 126-stale-lease scenario will measure only 16 leases and leave 110 as “NOT MEASURED”. That conflicts with the CONFORMANCE requirement that the new `lease.scan_view_trees_max` knob defaults to the old behaviour; old `status` measured every expired lease, so the default must be uncapped. Either conforming code fails this assertion, or the shipped default violates the requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py::test_recover_still_measures_every_tree

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `LC.brief` twice without setting `worktree.sweep_interval_s`, then asserts only one `sweep_finished` call. But the CONFORMANCE requirement says the new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to the old behaviour, where `brief` ran `sweep_finished` on every invocation; that default must therefore be `0`, and with `0` each of the two calls in this test invokes the patched `sweep_finished`, making `len(calls) == 2` and failing the assertion. If the default is positive to make this test pass, the build violates the stated conformance.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py::test_brief_sweeps_finished_worktrees_at_most_once_per_interval

chunk_findings.detail: `_sweep_stamp(repo)` is now called before `CL.sweep_finished`. If the derived stamp write fails (for example `.ddflow/local` is read-only or its parent is missing), the enclosing `except Exception: pass` swallows the error and `CL.sweep_finished` is never invoked, so finished worktrees are not swept at all. Before this change `CL.sweep_finished` ran first, so a stamp-write failure only caused a later retry; now a transient or permission problem with the stamp file can silently disable the sweep for the current and future due checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:240

chunk_findings.detail: The knob still defaults to `new = "900"`, while the old behaviour was a sweep on every brief (`0`). The added `why` text now labels this a "Default-behaviour change" and an exception to r-upgrade-safe, but the earlier finding cited r-everything-configurable ("a new knob defaults to the old behaviour"). The probe in the triage only counts git subprocesses for `status` and never exercises `brief`, so it does not refute this. In an upgraded repo with finished leftover worktrees and no `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last`, `ddflow brief` still skips the first sweep for up to 15 minutes where old code would have swept immediately.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The note now says "Default-behaviour change" in `why`, but all three modified upgrade notes still set `impact = "additive"`. A default-behaviour change for existing repos is not additive: an upgraded repo with 17 stale worktrees sees the 17th reported NOT MEASURED under the new default with no config change. Upgrade tooling that uses `impact` to classify breaking changes will not flag this note, which contradicts r-docs-with-change. The same mismatch is in `knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml` and `knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:impact

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `LC.brief` twice without setting `worktree.sweep_interval_s`, then asserts exactly one `sweep_finished` call. With the documented old-behaviour value `worktree.sweep_interval_s = 0`, every brief must run the sweeper, so `len(calls)` becomes 2 and the assertion fails. The test therefore depends on the new 900-second default and cannot pass in an environment that uses the knob value the upgrade note itself says restores the old behaviour; it should set the interval explicitly to a positive value before the two brief calls.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py:test_a_sweep_that_raises_is_not_retried_on_every_brief

chunk_findings.detail: The new test patches `leases.L.scan`, then calls `RP.health_lines(log, ..., repo, [])` with an explicit `recoveries=[]`. After this diff, `ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py` no longer imports or calls `leases.scan`, and the removed branch would only have run when `recoveries is None`, not for `[]`. Since `RP.health_lines` is `waitcycles.health_lines`, the spy is never invoked, `views` stays `[]`, and `assert views and not any(views), views` raises `AssertionError: []`. The test fails on the new code and cannot serve as a regression test.

chunk_findings.detail: `branch_tip_aheads` interpolates `base` directly into a `git for-each-ref` format atom with `f"--format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:{base})"`. Git branch/ref names may legally contain a closing parenthesis, e.g. `release/1.0)`. For a repo whose base branch has that name, the format becomes `%(ahead-behind:release/1.0))`; Git ends the atom at the first `)`, so it resolves the wrong ref or fails, and `branch_tip_aheads` returns `{}` instead of the real ahead counts. This is a regression for valid refnames compared with passing the base as a revision argument.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/git.py:branch_tip_aheads
